title: The Transfiguration and Faith
overview: Matthew 17 presents a profound revelation of Jesus’ divine glory through the Transfiguration, where He is seen speaking with Moses and Elijah, affirming His fulfillment of the Law and the Prophets. This chapter also addresses the nature of faith through the disciples’ inability to heal a demon-possessed boy, emphasizing the power of faith and prayer. Jesus foretells His suffering, death, and resurrection, preparing His disciples for the coming trials. The chapter concludes with a lesson on humility and provision through the miracle of the coin in the fish’s mouth. This passage highlights the intersection of divine glory, human faith, and obedience, reinforcing Jesus’ identity as the Son of God and the Messiah.
structure:
**Verses 1-9: The Transfiguration.** Jesus takes Peter, James, and John up a high mountain where He is transfigured, revealing His divine glory. Moses and Elijah appear, symbolizing the Law and the Prophets, and God’s voice affirms Jesus as His beloved Son.

**Verses 10-13: Discussion on Elijah’s Coming.** The disciples question Jesus about Elijah’s role, and He explains that John the Baptist fulfilled this prophecy, linking Old Testament expectations with His own mission.

**Verses 14-21: Healing of the Demon-Possessed Boy.** A man brings his afflicted son to Jesus after the disciples fail to heal him. Jesus rebukes the demon and teaches about the necessity of faith, prayer, and fasting for spiritual authority.

**Verses 22-23: Prediction of Jesus’ Death and Resurrection.** Jesus foretells His betrayal, death, and resurrection, preparing His disciples for the coming events.

**Verses 24-27: The Temple Tax and the Coin in the Fish’s Mouth.** Jesus teaches about freedom from earthly obligations for His followers and performs a miracle to pay the temple tax, demonstrating divine provision and humility.

keyVerses.text: While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.
keyVerses.significance: This verse is the divine affirmation of Jesus’ identity as God’s Son, confirming His authority and the importance of listening to Him. It anchors the Transfiguration as a pivotal moment revealing Jesus’ divine nature.

keyVerses.text: And Jesus said unto them, Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you.
keyVerses.significance: This verse highlights the power of even small faith to accomplish great things, emphasizing the necessity of trust in God for spiritual authority and miracles.

keyVerses.text: And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall be raised again. And they were exceeding sorry.
keyVerses.significance: Jesus’ clear prediction of His death and resurrection is central to Christian doctrine, preparing the disciples for the Messiah’s suffering and victory over death.

keyVerses.text: And Jesus rebuked the devil; and he departed out of him: and the child was cured from that very hour.
keyVerses.significance: This verse demonstrates Jesus’ authority over demonic forces and His power to heal, reinforcing His divine mission and compassion.

characters.name: Jesus Christ
characters.description: The central figure of the chapter, revealed in divine glory during the Transfiguration, teacher of faith and prayer, foreteller of His death and resurrection, and the one who exercises authority over demons and earthly matters.

characters.name: Peter
characters.description: One of Jesus’ closest disciples, present at the Transfiguration, who expresses the desire to build tabernacles for Jesus, Moses, and Elijah, showing his reverence and misunderstanding of the event’s significance.

characters.name: James and John
characters.description: Brothers and disciples of Jesus, witnesses to the Transfiguration, representing the inner circle of Jesus’ followers who receive special revelation.

characters.name: Moses and Elijah
characters.description: Representatives of the Law and the Prophets who appear with Jesus during the Transfiguration, symbolizing the fulfillment of Old Testament revelation in Christ.

characters.name: The Demon-Possessed Boy’s Father
characters.description: A desperate man seeking Jesus’ help for his afflicted son, illustrating human need and faith in Jesus’ power to heal.

themes.description: The Transfiguration reveals Jesus’ divine nature, shining light on His glory and affirming His identity as God’s Son, connecting the Old Testament with the New.
The disciples’ failure to heal the boy highlights the necessity of genuine faith and persistent prayer, underscoring spiritual dependence on God.
Jesus’ explanation of Elijah’s coming and His own prediction of death and resurrection show the fulfillment of Old Testament prophecy in His person and mission.
Jesus’ rebuke of the demon demonstrates His supreme authority over spiritual forces, reinforcing His role as Savior and Lord.
The temple tax episode teaches humility and trust in God’s provision, illustrating how believers navigate earthly responsibilities without offense.

historicalContext: This chapter takes place in first-century Galilee, a region under Roman occupation where Jewish religious expectations were high, especially concerning the coming Messiah. The high mountain setting for the Transfiguration reflects biblical traditions of divine revelation on mountains, such as Sinai. The presence of Moses and Elijah connects Jesus to the Jewish Law and Prophets, affirming His fulfillment of Scripture. The temple tax was a customary religious obligation for Jews, symbolizing their covenant relationship with God and support for temple worship. The political climate was tense, with Roman authority imposing taxes and religious leaders maintaining strict adherence to the Law, setting the stage for Jesus’ teachings on faith, authority, and obedience.

theologicalInterpretations.description: Reformed theology emphasizes the Transfiguration as a confirmation of Christ’s divine glory and the fulfillment of the Law and Prophets in Him. The call to faith and prayer reflects the necessity of reliance on God’s sovereign grace for spiritual power.

Dispensationalists see the Transfiguration as a future preview of Christ’s millennial reign, with Moses and Elijah representing the Law and Prophets that will be fully realized. The emphasis on faith and fasting is seen as part of the believer’s spiritual preparation.

Early Church Fathers interpreted the Transfiguration as a revelation of Christ’s divine nature to the disciples, strengthening their faith. They also viewed the healing and teachings on faith as practical instructions for Christian living and spiritual warfare.

crossReferences.connection: Peter recalls the Transfiguration as a powerful witness to Jesus’ divine glory, confirming the authenticity of the gospel message.
Luke’s parallel account of the Transfiguration provides additional details and emphasizes the voice from heaven affirming Jesus as God’s Son.
Mark’s version of the Transfiguration highlights the disciples’ fear and Jesus’ command to keep the vision secret until after His resurrection.
John’s declaration of the Word becoming flesh connects to the Transfiguration’s revelation of Jesus’ glory as the incarnate Son of God.
This passage contrasts the terrifying experience of Mount Sinai with the glorious revelation at Mount Zion, paralleling the Transfiguration event.
Prophecy about Elijah’s coming is fulfilled in John the Baptist, as Jesus explains in this chapter.

application: Trust God’s promises even when circumstances seem impossible, exercising faith like a mustard seed.
Engage in persistent prayer and fasting to strengthen spiritual authority and overcome challenges.
Recognize Jesus as the fulfillment of the Law and Prophets and submit to His teaching as God’s beloved Son.
Respond to spiritual needs with compassion and faith, seeking Jesus’ power to heal and deliver.
Practice humility and obedience in daily responsibilities, trusting God’s provision in all things.
conclusion: Matthew 17 powerfully reveals Jesus’ divine glory and authority, calling believers to a deeper faith marked by prayer, humility, and obedience. The Transfiguration affirms Jesus as the fulfillment of Scripture and God’s beloved Son, while the healing of the demon-possessed boy challenges believers to trust God’s power through faith. Jesus’ prediction of His death and resurrection prepares His followers for the cost of discipleship. The chapter’s lessons on faith, spiritual authority, and divine provision remain vital for Christians seeking to live faithfully in a challenging world.
timeline: c. AD 30 - Ministry of Jesus, including the Transfiguration and early Galilean ministry

definitions.definition: To be transformed in appearance, especially to reveal divine glory or majesty.
The Greek form of Elijah, the Old Testament prophet expected to return before the Messiah.
An archaic term meaning possessed by a demon or suffering from epilepsy or mental illness, as understood in biblical times.
Temporary shelters or booths, often used during Jewish festivals to commemorate the wilderness dwelling of Israel.
A tax or payment required by governing authorities, in this context the temple tax paid by Jewish men for the upkeep of the temple.
